intro.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a program that reconstructs a travel itinerary from a list of flight tickets, ensuring you visit all destinations exactly once in the correct order. You will learn to use depth-first search (DFS), a fundamental graph traversal algorithm, to explore possible routes and find the valid itinerary. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, objects (for adjacency lists), and recursion or a stack for DFS implementation. By the end, you will understand how to model problems as graphs and apply DFS to solve path-finding challenges in a beginner-friendly way.
intro.usecase: The Reconstruct Itinerary algorithm is essential in travel and logistics applications, such as flight booking systems or trip planners, where users have multiple tickets and need to find a valid travel sequence. For example, a dashboard in a travel app might use this to display a user's complete journey from scattered flight segments, ensuring no airport is visited out of order. Developers implement this to handle complex routing data, similar to how package delivery services optimize multi-stop routes from a set of delivery points.
